task_message:
Case N09: segment the peripheral nerve sheath tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 280x280x231 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
Case N09 is complete.

**Summary:** The peripheral nerve sheath tumor is a large, well-circumscribed T2-hyperintense mass with a heterogeneous ("target-like") centre in the subcutaneous/deep fascial compartment. I seeded it with two positive points on an axial slice through its largest cross-section, then ran a model refinement that cleaned the boundary and removed stray specks (final mask: single component, 125.8 mL, axial 96–197, coronal 101–151, sagittal 155–211).

**Verification:** The green outline was checked slice-by-slice in all three planes (axial 100–196, coronal 114–138, sagittal 147–197). The five-slice end-review panels showed no remaining lesion beyond the mask ends, and the automatic candidates (C1–C3) were all subcutaneous fat crescents along the skin surface, so none were accepted. Only residual uncertainty is a thin bright fascial/nerve extension inferiorly, which is partly included — hence medium confidence.
